mainTopic: Whether designation (הזמנה) counts, who inherits from people executed by the king, and how דוד's curses on יואב came true in דוד's line
overview: Earlier on this daf, אביי held that setting an item aside (הזמנה) for a purpose already gives it that status, while רבא held that only actual use counts. The גמרא rejects a proof for רבא from clothes thrown on a bier, and explains with עולא that the ban there is only so people won't confuse them with shrouds. A proof for אביי from a pouch for תפילין is rejected by reading it like רב חסדא. A ברייתא about a case for a ספר תורה seems to support רבא, but the גמרא says the question is an older argument among תנאים. After רבא shows that a garment woven after death really happens, as in הרפניא, the גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רבא. Then a new ברייתא argues whether the property of people executed by the king goes to the king or to the heirs. The גמרא tests this with נבות's vineyard and with יואב grabbing the מזבח, and turns the proofs aside. The story of יואב leads to רב's teaching that דוד's curses on יואב came true in דוד's own descendants: רחבעם, עוזיהו, אסא, יאשיהו and יכניה. The explanation of יכניה's curse continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The clothes thrown on the bier were thrown out of grief
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבא from the parents who threw clothes on their son's bier. They acted out of bitterness, not real intent to give the clothes to the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because of their bitterness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier proof for רבא. It says the bier case does not prove that הזמנה means nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis allowed the clothes to be saved. That does not show that setting aside is meaningless. The parents never truly meant to set the clothes aside for the dead. They threw them in a moment of grief, so there was no real הזמנה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: setting an item aside for a specific purpose

phrases.english: There, it is because of their bitterness.
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the parents who threw clothes onto their son's bier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רבא brought just before this passage from the bier ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of the bier ברייתא as a proof that הזמנה is meaningless.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The parents' act came from grief, not real intent, so the case contains no true הזמנה.

steps.title: Why would clothes that touched the bier be forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: If grief-driven throwing means nothing, the גמרא asks how to explain רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He says clothes that already touched the bier are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how do you explain what is taught about it: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said, when is this said? When the clothes did not touch the bier. But if they touched the bier, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection from step 1. It points to a line in the same ברייתא that seems to give the parents' act real weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the parents' throwing was meaningless grief. But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids the clothes once they touch the bier. That suggests the act did create a status. So how can we call it empty?

keyTerms.meaning: if so, if that is true
in what case is this said? (limits a ruling)

phrases.english: If so, how is this that is taught about it:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said?
Where they did not touch the bier,
but if they touched the bier, they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'it was just grief' rejection in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 1 that the parents' act out of bitterness has no legal weight.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the act meant nothing, touching the bier should not make the clothes forbidden. Yet רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids them.

steps.title: עולא: the bier is buried with him, so people might confuse the clothes with shrouds
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the case is a bier that gets buried with the dead person. The clothes on it could be mistaken for shrouds (תכריכין), so the rabbis forbade them as a safeguard.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא explained it: it is about a bier that is buried with him, since the clothes could be mixed up with the shrouds of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 2. The ban is not because the parents' act made the clothes forbidden. It is a rabbinic safeguard against confusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real shrouds of the dead are forbidden for benefit. If clothes that touched a bier being buried with the dead were allowed, people might think shrouds are allowed too. So the ban is about appearances, and the parents' grief-driven act still carries no weight. The rejection in step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: he explained it, he interpreted it
they could be mixed up, mistaken
the shrouds of the dead person

steps.whatToRemember: The bier case proves nothing about הזמנה. The parents acted out of grief. The ban on clothes that touched the bier is only a safeguard so people do not confuse them with shrouds.

phrases.english: Ulla explained it:
With a bier that is buried with him,
since they could be mistaken for the shrouds of the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 and saves the rejection in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ruling refers to a specific case where a rabbinic safeguard applies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Touching the bier made the clothes truly forbidden, so the parents' act had legal weight.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is only a גזירה because the clothes may be confused with real shrouds. The parents' act itself means nothing.

steps.title: A pouch made for תפילין may not hold money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support אביי. A pouch made for תפילין may not hold money, but a pouch that just happened to hold תפילין may.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a pouch that someone made to put תפילין in may not have money put in it. If he put תפילין in it, he may put money in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt, this time to prove אביי's view that הזמנה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is only about making the pouch for תפילין, and it is already forbidden for money. That sounds like setting aside alone is enough. The second case shows that using without setting aside first does not forbid it. So it seems the setting aside is what counts, just like אביי says.

keyTerms.meaning: the leather boxes with פרשיות worn on the head and arm

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A pouch that he made to put tefillin in it –
it is forbidden to put money in it.

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחַ בּוֹ תְּפִילִּין – יַנִּיחַ בּוֹ מָעוֹת.
phrases.english: If he put tefillin in it, he may put money in it.
phrases.notes: This means he used it for תפילין without having made or set it aside for them first.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כִּיס שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ לְהַנִּיחַ בּוֹ תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bier proof for רבא fell away, the גמרא now tries a proof for אביי.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that הזמנה alone gives an item its status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a pouch made for תפילין is forbidden for money, but one merely used for תפילין is not.

steps.title: Read it as: made for תפילין and also used for them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. It reads the ברייתא as a pouch that was both made for תפילין and then actually used for them, matching רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: he made it and put תפילין in it. Then it is forbidden to put money in it, like רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for אביי by rereading the first case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is not from setting aside alone. It needs setting aside plus real use. That is רב חסדא's rule from earlier on the daf, and רבא can accept it. So the ברייתא no longer proves that הזמנה by itself counts.

keyTerms.meaning: say, read it as (rereads a source)
he made it and he put (both steps)
in line with רב חסדא's ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second case of the ברייתא is now the same as the first. The first case is made for תפילין plus used, so it is forbidden. The second case is used for תפילין with no setting aside, so it is permitted.

phrases.english: Say: he made it and put tefillin in it –
it is forbidden to put money in it,
in accordance with Rav Chisda.
phrases.notes: This points back to רב חסדא earlier on the daf. A cloth set aside for תפילין and then actually used for them can't hold money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for אביי offered in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of the pouch ברייתא as a proof that הזמנה alone counts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as needing both setting aside and actual use, which fits רבא.

steps.title: A case ordered for a ספר or תפילין stays ordinary until used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבא. A case or bag ordered for a ספר תורה or תפילין may be used for ordinary things until it is actually used for the holy item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone told a craftsman, 'Make me a case for a ספר' or 'a bag for תפילין,' then until he uses them for something holy, he may use them for ordinary things. Once he uses them for something holy, he may not use them for ordinary things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a new source to prove רבא's view that setting aside alone means nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the item was clearly ordered for a holy purpose, which is real הזמנה. Even so, it stays permitted for ordinary use until it is actually used for the holy item. This looks like strong support for רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: This ברייתא seems to back רבא: an item ordered for holy use stays ordinary until it is actually used for that holy purpose.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְאוּמָּן ״עֲשֵׂה לִי תִּיק שֶׁל סֵפֶר״
phrases.english: If one said to a craftsman, "Make me a case for a scroll"
or "a bag for tefillin" –
as long as he has not used them for something holy,
it is permitted to use them for ordinary things.
Once he has used them for something holy –
it is forbidden to use them for ordinary things.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָמַר לְאוּמָּן עֲשֵׂה לִי תִּיק שֶׁל סֵפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for אביי was rejected, the גמרא tries a new proof for רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that הזמנה alone does not give an item its status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a case or bag ordered from a craftsman for holy use stays permitted for ordinary use until it is actually used for something holy.

steps.title: The designation question is already a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the argument between אביי and רבא about whether mere designation matters already appears as an argument in a ברייתא about patching תפילין with animal hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute among תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if someone covered תפילין with gold, or patched them with the hide of a non-kosher animal, they are invalid. If he used the hide of a kosher animal, they are valid, even though he did not process the hide for the sake of the מצוה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even with a kosher animal's hide they are invalid, until he processes it for the sake of the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the proof for רבא in step 6, the גמרא says the question is really an older argument among תנאים. So the ברייתא in step 6 follows one תנא, and אביי can follow the other. The גמרא then quotes the ברייתא that shows this argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the hide does not need to be processed לשמה, so preparing it for the מצוה adds nothing. This matches רבא, who says designation alone is nothing. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires processing לשמה, which is like saying designation matters, and this matches אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
He processed the hides for the sake of the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. The one who requires processing לשמה (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) is the one who matches אביי, since he holds that preparing something for a purpose matters.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim, as it is taught:
phrases.notes: "It" means the argument between אביי and רבא about whether just designating something matters.

phrases.english: If one coated them with gold
phrases.notes: "Them" means תפילין.

phrases.english: or patched onto them
the hide of a non-kosher animal, they are unfit.
With the hide of a kosher animal, they are fit,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא עִיבְּדָן לִשְׁמָן.
phrases.english: even though he did not process them for their sake.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even with the hide of a kosher animal they are unfit,
until he processes it for their sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the proof for רבא in step 6: the issue is an older dispute among תנאים, so that ברייתא does not settle it against אביי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether designation alone matters is a dispute between the תנא קמא (like רבא) and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (like אביי).

steps.title: Does anyone really weave a garment after death
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא whether there is actually a place where the dead are laid out first and only afterward a garment is woven for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: Is there really a place where they lay out a dead person and only then weave a garment for him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a practical question about the earlier case of a garment woven for a dead person: does that situation ever really happen?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally shrouds are ready ahead of time, so a garment woven after death seems unlikely. רבינא wants to know if the argument about such a garment is realistic.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Is there a place
where they lay out a dead person,
and then weave a garment for the dead?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier argument about a garment woven for a dead person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the case of a garment woven for the dead, asking whether it is realistic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a real situation where a garment is woven for a dead person only after he dies.

steps.title: Yes, like the dead of הרפניא
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that yes, this happens, for example with the dead of הרפניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, for example the dead of הרפניא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבינא's question by giving a real example of a place where this happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By naming a real place, רבא shows that the case is practical and not just theory. So the argument about such a garment has real-world use.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
for example, the dead of Harpanya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, כְּגוֹן שָׁכְבֵי דְּהַרְפַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. In places like הרפניא, garments are woven for the dead after death.

steps.title: Two opinions on whose view is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught that the הלכה follows אביי, while the רבנן said it follows רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: the הלכה follows אביי. The רבנן say: the הלכה follows רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports two different rulings about whose view is the final הלכה. This sets up the final decision in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following אביי means designation alone has legal force. Following רבא means only actual use counts. Since the rulings conflict, the גמרא still needs to decide.

phrases.english: Mareimar taught:
The halacha is like Abaye,
and the Rabbis say:
The halacha is like Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analysis to practical ruling on the אביי–רבא dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרימר rules like אביי, and the רבנן rule like רבא.

steps.title: Final ruling follows רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא decides that the הלכה follows רבא: designation alone does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final decision between the two rulings: the הלכה follows רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in practice, just designating an item does not give it a new status. Only actual use does. For example, a garment only becomes forbidden once it is actually used for the dead.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה follows רבא: mere designation (הזמנה) does nothing. Only actual use changes an item's status.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two conflicting rulings of step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבא: designation alone has no legal effect.

steps.title: Who gets the property of executed people
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: the property of people executed by the king goes to the king, and the property of people executed by בית דין goes to their heirs. רבי יהודה says even הרוגי מלכות leave their property to their heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: people executed by the king, their property goes to the king. People executed by בית דין, their property goes to their heirs. רבי יהודה says: even for people executed by the king, their property goes to the heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a brand-new topic with a ברייתא about inheritance after an execution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of execution: by the king (for rebelling against him) and by בית דין (for a sin). The חכמים give the king the property in the first case. רבי יהודה says the heirs always inherit.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Those executed by the king, their property goes to the king;
those executed by the court, their property goes to the heirs.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even those executed by the king, their property goes to the heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת נִכְסֵיהֶן לַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, unrelated to the designation discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים give the property of הרוגי מלכות to the king, and of הרוגי בית דין to the heirs. רבי יהודה gives both to the heirs.

steps.title: Challenge from נבות's vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי יהודה from the פסוק saying אחאב went down to נבות's vineyard "to inherit it."
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי יהודה: But isn't it already written, "Behold, he is in the vineyard of נבות, where he went down to inherit it"?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי יהודה's view with a פסוק that seems to show the king does take the property of people he executes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבות was killed by the king's order, and the פסוק calls אחאב's taking of the vineyard "inheriting." That suggests the king had a legal right to the property, against רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: To inherit it / take possession of it

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
But isn't it already stated:
"Behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 21:18

phrases.english: where he went down to inherit it"?
phrases.notes: The word "inherit" is the key: it sounds like אחאב had a real right to the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's view from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the heirs inherit even from הרוגי מלכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes אחאב as "inheriting" the vineyard of נבות, whom the king had executed. That implies the king legally gets the property.

steps.title: אחאב inherited נבות as a relative
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that אחאב was נבות's cousin and took the vineyard as an heir, not as king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to them: אחאב was the son of נבות's father's brother, so he was fit to inherit from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה defends himself against the חכמים' proof from the פסוק about אחאב 'inheriting' the vineyard. He says אחאב inherited it because he was family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים read 'to inherit it' as meaning the king takes the property of הרוגי מלכות. רבי יהודה reads the same word literally: אחאב was a real heir, a cousin. So the פסוק fits his view that the property goes to the heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to them (רבי יהודה answering the חכמים)
His father's brother's son, a first cousin

phrases.english: He said to them:
He was the son of his father's brother,
phrases.notes: He means אחאב was נבות's first cousin.

phrases.english: and he was fit to inherit from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: בֶּן אֲחִי אָבִיו הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' challenge from the פסוק about נבות's vineyard.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: 'inherit' means real family inheritance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחאב took the vineyard because the king gets the property of הרוגי מלכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: אחאב took it as נבות's cousin and legal heir.

steps.title: But נבות had many sons
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים object that נבות had sons, and they would inherit before a cousin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't נבות have many sons?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's answer. A cousin cannot inherit when there are sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sons come before cousins in inheritance. If נבות had sons, אחאב as a cousin could not have been the heir. So the 'cousin' answer seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: But did he not have many sons?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהודה's cousin answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that אחאב inherited as a cousin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sons inherit before a cousin, and נבות had many sons.

steps.title: אחאב killed נבות's sons too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that אחאב killed נבות and his sons, and he brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: אחאב killed נבות and his sons, as the פסוק says: 'Surely I have seen the blood of נבות and the blood of his sons.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the question about the sons. They were killed as well, so the cousin was next in line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the sons were dead, nobody closer than אחאב was left. So אחאב really was the heir. The פסוק mentions 'the blood of his sons', which shows they were killed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated (a proof from a פסוק)

phrases.english: He said to them:
He killed him and his sons,
as it is stated:
"Surely the blood of Naboth
and the blood of his sons I have seen."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ט:כו

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about נבות's sons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New fact from a פסוק: the sons were killed too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נבות's living sons should have inherited.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sons were also killed, so the cousin אחאב inherited.

steps.title: How do the חכמים read that פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים deal with the פסוק about the blood of נבות's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים, how do they explain this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks how the חכמים handle רבי יהודה's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to support רבי יהודה's claim that the sons were killed. The חכמים need their own reading of it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the חכמים: how do they deal with this?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי יהודה's proof back to the חכמים for their response.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the חכמים understand 'the blood of his sons'.

steps.title: The verse means his future children
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים read 'his sons' as the children נבות would have had in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is talking about the sons who would have come from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the חכמים' reading. 'The blood of his sons' means the children נבות never got to have because he was killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, נבות's actual sons were not necessarily killed. So they would have inherited, and אחאב could not have taken the vineyard as an heir. That keeps the חכמים' proof alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who were fit to come out from him (future children)

phrases.english: That refers to sons
who were fit to come out from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'His sons' means the children נבות would have had, not living sons who were killed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says אחאב was the heir because he killed נבות and his sons. The חכמים say the פסוק means future children, so אחאב took the vineyard as king.

steps.title: Why did the witnesses add 'and king'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: the witnesses said נבות cursed 'God and king'. Why mention the king, unless it was to let the king take the property?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the view that their property goes to the king, since it says 'נבות cursed God and king'. But according to the view that the property goes to the heirs, why mention 'king'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof against רבי יהודה from the wording of the false testimony against נבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the king takes the property of הרוגי מלכות, the plotters needed נבות to be guilty of cursing the king so the vineyard would go to אחאב. According to רבי יהודה, cursing God alone would have been enough. So the extra word 'king' seems pointless for him.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
That is why it is written
Literally 'blessed', a polite way of saying 'cursed'

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says
their property goes to the king,
that is why it is written
"Naboth cursed God and king."
phrases.notes: מלכים א כא:יג. The word literally says 'blessed', but it's a polite way of saying 'cursed'.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
their property goes to the heirs,
why do I need "and king"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר נִכְסֵיהֶן לַמֶּלֶךְ, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי יהודה, separate from the 'to inherit it' proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the property of הרוגי מלכות goes to the heirs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding 'and king' only helps if the king takes the property of someone he executes.

steps.title: Both charges were to stir up anger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both 'God' and 'king' were said only to make the judges angrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, why mention 'God'? You must say it was to increase the anger. So too, 'king' was there to increase the anger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by turning it around. The other side also has an extra word to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the king takes the property, cursing the king would be enough, so 'God' looks extra. The challenger must admit 'God' was added just to make נבות look worse. רבי יהודה can say the same thing about 'king', so the proof falls away.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
why do I need "God"?
Rather, it was to increase the anger.
So too, it was to increase the anger.
phrases.notes: He means the word 'king' was also added just to make the judges angrier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away the 'God and king' proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the question around: both sides have an extra word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'And king' was added so the king could take the property.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'And king' was added only to make the judges angrier, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: Why did יואב hold on to the מזבח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another proof: יואב held on to the altar and said 'here I will die'. That makes sense if he wanted to keep his property away from the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the view that the property goes to the king. That is why יואב ran to the משכן, grabbed the horns of the altar and said 'I will not leave, for here I will die.' But according to the view that the property goes to the heirs, what difference did it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof for the view that the king takes the property of הרוגי מלכות. It uses יואב's behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the king's execution means the king gets your property, יואב wanted to die some other way so his family would keep it. According to רבי יהודה, the heirs get the property anyway. So why did יואב care how he died?

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says:
"their property goes to the king,"
that is why it is written:
"And Joab fled to the tent of ה׳
and took hold of the horns of the altar,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א ב:כח

phrases.english: and it is written:
"And he said: I will not go out, for here I will die."
phrases.notes: מלכים א ב:ל

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
"their property goes to the heirs,"
what difference did it make to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: ״נִכְסֵיהֶן לַמֶּלֶךְ״, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate proof against רבי יהודה, using the same 'בשלמא' pattern.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that the property of הרוגי מלכות goes to the heirs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יואב's effort to avoid being executed by the king only makes sense if the king would take his property.

steps.title: יואב just wanted to live a little longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that יואב held on to the altar only to gain a little more time to live.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did it to gain a little more life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the יואב proof. יואב's reason had nothing to do with his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding the altar delayed his death, and that alone is a good enough reason. So יואב's behavior does not prove who gets the property. The dispute between the חכמים and רבי יהודה stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: For a short stretch of life

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs from the פסוקים, 'God and king' and יואב at the altar, are turned away. The dispute over the property of הרוגי מלכות is not settled by them.

phrases.english: For a short while of life.
phrases.notes: He means יואב held the altar just to stay alive a little longer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away the יואב proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another reason for his actions: he wanted to delay death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יואב refused to be executed by the king so that his property would not go to the king.
steps.terutzMaskana: יואב just wanted to live a bit longer, so nothing is proven about the property.

steps.title: יואב's message to שלמה: you can't have it both ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what יואב told בניהו to tell שלמה: if you kill me, you take on דוד's curses against me. If you don't want them, let me live and carry them myself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says בניהו brought the king word of what יואב said. יואב told him: Go tell שלמה that he can't do two things to me. If he kills me, he must accept the curses his father put on me. If he won't accept them, he should leave me alive so I carry those curses myself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the details behind a short פסוק: what exactly יואב told בניהו to report to שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד had cursed יואב and his family. יואב argues that if שלמה kills him, the curses can no longer land on יואב, so they will move to שלמה's family. This is יואב's bargaining move to stay alive.

keyTerms.meaning: בניהו בן יהוידע, the man שלמה sent to kill יואב

phrases.english: "And Benaiah brought the king word back, saying:
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:30

phrases.english: So said Joab, and so he answered me."
He said to him: Go say to him:
phrases.notes: יואב is talking to בניהו, and "him" at the end is שלמה.

phrases.english: You cannot do two things to this man.
phrases.notes: "This man" is יואב talking about himself.

phrases.english: If you kill him,
accept the curses that your father cursed him with.
And if not, leave him alone
so that he may carry the curses that your father cursed him with.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of יואב at the מזבח by explaining what the reply in the פסוק actually was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יואב warned that killing him would move דוד's curses onto שלמה's family.

steps.title: שלמה answers: do as he said and kill him
steps.stepSummary: שלמה tells בניהו to do as יואב said, strike him down, and bury him. He accepts the curses on his own family.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king said to him: Do as he said. Strike him down and bury him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שלמה's reply from the next פסוק. This sets up רב's teaching that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read with יואב's message, "do as he has said" means שלמה chose the first option: kill יואב and take on the curses. That is why the next step can say the curses came true in דוד's descendants.

phrases.english: "And the king said to him:
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:31

phrases.english: Do as he has said,
and strike him down and bury him."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ עֲשֵׂה כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שלמה's answer to יואב's message.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה accepted the curses and had יואב killed.

steps.title: All of דוד's curses on יואב came true in דוד's family
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב teaches that every curse דוד said against יואב came true in דוד's own descendants. He quotes the list of curses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: All the curses דוד put on יואב came true in דוד's descendants. The curse was: "Let the house of יואב never be without a זב, a מצורע, one who leans on a staff, one who falls by the sword, and one who lacks bread."
steps.whatsHappening: רב makes a big claim and quotes the פסוק with five curses. This sets up the next steps, which prove each curse one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because שלמה accepted the curses when he had יואב killed, they moved to דוד's family. The פסוק lists five curses, and the גמרא will now find a descendant of דוד for each.

keyTerms.meaning: one who holds a staff (or spindle)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the plan for the rest of the section: each curse in the list will be matched to a king from דוד's line.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל קְלָלוֹת שֶׁקִּילֵּל דָּוִד אֶת יוֹאָב
phrases.english: All the curses with which David cursed Joab
came true in David's descendants.
"Let the house of Joab never be without
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 3:29

phrases.english: one with a discharge, or a leper,
or one who holds onto a staff,
or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on שלמה accepting the curses and says what happened to them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every curse דוד placed on יואב came true in דוד's descendants.

steps.title: The curse of זב came true in רחבעם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רחבעם was a זב by linking the word מרכבה (chariot) in his story to the word מרכב (saddle) in the laws of a זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: "זב" came true in רחבעם. It says: "King רחבעם hurried to get up into the מרכבה (chariot) to run to ירושלים." And it says about a זב: "Any מרכב (saddle) that the זב rides on becomes טמא."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first curse, זב, came true in a king from דוד's line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים use almost the same word: מרכבה for רחבעם and מרכב for the זב. That shared word is the hint that רחבעם was a זב.

keyTerms.meaning: a man with a certain bodily discharge that makes him טמא

phrases.english: "A zav" came true in Rehoboam, as it is written:
"And King Rehoboam hurried
to get up into the chariot to flee to Jerusalem,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 12:18

phrases.english: and it is written: "And any saddle
that the zav rides on becomes impure."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:9. Notice the shared word, מרכבה and מרכב. That's the link.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving רב's claim, starting with the first curse on the list.
steps.raayaObject: That the curse of זב came true in דוד's line
steps.raayaSupportSource: The matching words מרכבה (מלכים א 12:18) and מרכב (ויקרא 15:9)

steps.title: The curse of צרעת came true in עוזיהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the curse of מצורע came true in עוזיהו, who went into the היכל to burn קטורת and was struck with צרעת on his forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: "מצורע" came true in עוזיהו. It says: "When he became strong, his heart grew proud until it ruined him. He betrayed ה' his God and went into the היכל of ה' to burn קטורת on the incense מזבח." And it says: "And צרעת broke out on his forehead."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second curse, מצורע, came true in another king from דוד's line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no word hint. The פסוקים say outright that עוזיהו got צרעת after he went in to burn קטורת, which was not his job.

keyTerms.meaning: a king of יהודה from דוד's line

steps.whatToRemember: רב says all of דוד's curses on יואב landed on דוד's own family, because שלמה accepted them. So far: זב from רחבעם, מצורע from עוזיהו.

phrases.english: "A leper" came true in Uzziah, as it is written:
"But when he was strong, his heart grew proud until it ruined him,
and he betrayed the Lord his God,
and he went into the Sanctuary of the Lord
to burn incense on the altar of incense,"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 26:16

phrases.english: and it is written: "And leprosy broke out on his forehead."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 26:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second curse on the list, following the same pattern as the זב proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the curse of מצורע came true in דוד's line
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 26:16 and 26:19 about עוזיהו

steps.title: The curse of holding a staff came true in אסא
steps.stepSummary: The curse 'holds onto a staff' came true in אסא, who was diseased in his feet in old age. רב יהודה in the name of רב says it was gout (פודגרא).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Holds onto a staff': this came true in אסא, as it is written: 'But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.' And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: he was seized with gout.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next curse on the list and shows it came true in King אסא. A פסוק says his feet were diseased, and רב explains it was gout.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who needs a staff to walk is someone with weak or painful legs. The פסוק says אסא's feet were diseased, so he fits this curse. רב adds which disease it was: פודגרא, a painful sickness of the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds onto a staff (needs a cane to walk)
A king of יהודה from דוד's line
Gout, a painful disease of the feet

phrases.english: "Holds onto a staff" came true in אסא,
phrases.notes: This is the next curse from דוד's list in Step 25.

phrases.english: as it is written: "But in the time of his old age
he was diseased in his feet."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 15:23

phrases.english: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
that he was seized with gout.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of curses from Step 25, after זב (Step 26) and מצורע (Step 27).
steps.raayaObject: That the curse of 'holding a staff' came true in דוד's descendants
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 15:23, which says אסא was diseased in his feet, explained by רב as gout

steps.title: מר זוטרא asks what gout is like
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, son of רב נחמן, asks his father what this disease is like.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא the son of רב נחמן said to רב נחמן: What is it like?
steps.whatsHappening: A side question comes up: מר זוטרא asks his father רב נחמן what gout feels like. This sets up רב נחמן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge to רב. It is just a request for more detail about the disease רב named.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? / What does it look like?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: מר זוטרא the son of רב נחמן said
to רב נחמן: What is it like?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן לְרַב נַחְמָן הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a description of the disease רב named in Step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the pain of פודגרא feels like

steps.title: רב נחמן: like a needle in living flesh
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that gout feels like a needle stuck in living flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Like a needle in living flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers his son: the pain of gout is like a needle piercing living flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how painful the curse was for אסא. It was not a mild weakness but sharp, stabbing pain.

phrases.english: He said to him: Like a needle in living flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pain is like a needle piercing living flesh

steps.title: How did רב נחמן know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן knew what gout feels like.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן could describe the pain so exactly. This sets up three possible answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Describing a feeling from the inside is surprising, so the גמרא wants to know his source. It is a curious question, not an attack on his words.

phrases.english: How did he know?
phrases.notes: "He" is רב נחמן, who just described the pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source of רב נחמן's description in Step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of רב נחמן's knowledge of the pain of gout

steps.title: Three possible ways רב נחמן knew
steps.stepSummary: Three answers: he suffered from it himself, he learned it from his teacher, or ה׳ revealed it to him, as the פסוק says 'The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: he himself suffered from it. And if you want, say: he learned it from his teacher. And if you want, say: 'The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him, and He will make His covenant known to them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three possible answers to how רב נחמן knew, and does not pick one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is personal experience. The second is a tradition passed down from his teacher. The third is that ה׳ shows hidden things to people who fear Him, proven from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of several possible answers)
The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives three options for how רב נחמן knew: he felt it himself, he learned it from his teacher, or ה׳ revealed it to him.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
he himself suffered from it.
And if you want, say:
he learned it from his teacher.
And if you want, say:
"The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him,
and He will make His covenant known to them."
phrases.notes: תהלים 25:14. The idea is that ה׳ showed him this, without his feeling it or being taught it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא מֵיחַשׁ הֲוָה חָיֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31 and closes the side discussion about gout.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three options: personal experience, a tradition from his teacher, or divine revelation (תהלים 25:14)

steps.title: The curse of falling by the sword came true in יאשיהו
steps.stepSummary: The curse 'falls by the sword' came true in יאשיהו, who was shot by archers. רב יהודה in the name of רב says they made his whole body like a sieve.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Falls by the sword': this came true in יאשיהו, as it is written: 'And the archers shot at King יאשיהו.' And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: they made his whole body like a sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of curses and shows that 'falling by the sword' came true in King יאשיהו, who was killed in battle by archers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says archers shot him, which means a violent death in war, matching the curse. רב adds how terrible it was: so many arrows hit him that his body was full of holes like a sieve.

keyTerms.meaning: Falls by the sword (dies violently in battle)
A king of יהודה from דוד's line

phrases.english: "Falls by the sword" came true in יאשיהו,
as it is written: "And the archers shot
at King יאשיהו."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 35:23

phrases.english: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
that they made his whole body like a sieve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion about gout to the list of curses from Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That the curse of 'falling by the sword' came true in דוד's descendants
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 35:23, the archers shooting יאשיהו, with רב's description of his body like a sieve

steps.title: The curse of lacking bread is linked to יכניה
steps.stepSummary: The curse 'lacks bread' is linked to יכניה, about whom the פסוק says he was given a steady food allowance. רב יהודה in the name of רב begins to explain this with a popular saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And lacks bread': this came true in יכניה, as it is written: 'And his food allowance was a steady allowance given to him.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is what people say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the last curse, 'lacking bread,' in King יכניה. It then starts to bring a popular saying from רב to explain it; the saying itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first this seems strange: the פסוק says יכניה was given steady food, not that he lacked bread. That puzzle is why רב brings a well-known saying, which will explain how being fed this way still counts as 'lacking bread.'

keyTerms.meaning: A king of יהודה from דוד's line, taken into exile
This is what people say (introduces a popular saying)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the פסוק proves יכניה had plenty and so the curse failed. The גמרא knows it looks that way, and the saying in the next line explains how this still fits 'lacking bread.'

phrases.english: "And lacks bread" came true in יכניה,
as it is written: "And his food allowance
was a steady allowance given to him."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 25:30. The king of בבל fed him, so he lived on another man's handouts.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
This is what people say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next curse on the list after 'falling by the sword' in Step 33.
steps.raayaObject: That the curse of 'lacking bread' came true in דוד's descendants
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 25:30, about יכניה's steady food allowance, about to be explained by a popular saying from רב
